recipes.name: Kottu Roti
recipes.shortDescription: Chopped godhamba roti stir-fried with curry, egg, and spices — Sri Lanka's iconic street food.
steps: Heat oil in a large wok or flat pan over medium-high heat.
Add onions, green chilies, and curry leaves. Sauté until fragrant and soft.
Add the chopped roti and toss continuously for 2–3 minutes.
Push the roti to one side of the pan, pour in the eggs, and scramble.
Mix the scrambled egg through the roti.
Add the chicken curry and toss everything together until well combined.
Adjust salt, and serve hot with pol sambol.

recipes.name: Rice and Curry
recipes.shortDescription: Sri Lanka's everyday meal — steamed rice with an array of curries, papadam, and sambol.
steps: Cook rice in a rice cooker or pot with 1.5x water.
Wash dhal and boil with turmeric and salt until soft.
In a pan, heat oil, add onion, green chilies, and curry leaves.
Add curry powder, then the cooked dhal and coconut milk.
Simmer for 10 minutes until thick and creamy.
Serve rice with dhal curry, papadam, and pol sambol.

recipes.name: Hoppers (Appa)
recipes.shortDescription: Bowl-shaped fermented rice flour pancakes with crispy edges — a Sri Lankan breakfast essential.
steps: Mix rice flour, yeast, sugar, and warm water into a smooth batter.
Cover and let ferment overnight (or 6–8 hours).
Stir in coconut milk and salt. Adjust consistency to thin pancake batter.
Heat a small wok or hopper pan. Pour a ladle of batter and swirl to coat edges.
Cover and cook until edges are crispy and center is set.
For egg hoppers, crack an egg into the center before covering.
Serve hot with pol sambol or a curry.

recipes.name: Kiribath (Milk Rice)
recipes.shortDescription: Creamy coconut milk rice — the ceremonial dish of Sri Lankan celebrations.
steps: Wash rice and cook with water until fully soft and water is absorbed.
Add coconut milk and salt. Stir gently.
Cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, until creamy and thick.
Spread onto a flat tray or banana leaf, about 1-inch thick.
Let cool and set, then cut into diamond shapes.
Serve with lunu miris or a spicy sambol.

recipes.name: Pol Sambol
recipes.shortDescription: Fresh coconut relish with chili, lime, and shallots — the essential Sri Lankan condiment.
ingredients: 2 dried red chilies (or 1 tsp chili powder)
steps: In a bowl, combine grated coconut, onion, and chilies.
Add chili powder (or crushed dried chilies).
Squeeze in the lime juice and add salt.
Mix well with clean hands or a spoon until the coconut turns pinkish.
Serve fresh with rice, hoppers, or string hoppers.

recipes.name: Pol Roti
recipes.shortDescription: Coconut flatbread — hearty, chewy, and perfect with a spicy sambol.
steps: Mix flour, coconut, onion, chilies, curry leaves, and salt.
Add water gradually and knead into a soft dough.
Divide into small balls and flatten into thin rounds.
Cook on a hot griddle until brown spots appear on both sides.
Serve warm with pol sambol or butter.

recipes.name: String Hoppers (Idiyappam)
recipes.shortDescription: Steamed rice flour noodles shaped into delicate nests — served with curry or sambol.
steps: Mix rice flour, salt, and hot water into a soft dough.
Add oil and knead until smooth.
Fill a string hopper press (idiya appam maker) with dough.
Press onto small woven mats in a circular motion.
Steam for 5–7 minutes until cooked.
Serve warm with kiri hodi (coconut milk curry) or pol sambol.

recipes.name: Helapa
recipes.shortDescription: Traditional Sri Lankan sweet — rice flour, treacle, and coconut steamed in kenda leaves.
ingredients: Kenda leaves (or banana leaves) for wrapping
steps: Mix rice flour, treacle, coconut, and cardamom into a thick batter.
Wash and soften kenda leaves.
Place a spoonful of batter on each leaf and fold into a parcel.
Arrange parcels in a steamer.
Steam for 25–30 minutes until firm.
Cool slightly before unwrapping. Serve with Ceylon tea.

recipes.name: Aasmi
recipes.shortDescription: Crispy, colorful New Year sweet — rice flour lace drizzled with pink syrup.
steps: Mix rice flour and coconut milk into a thin batter.
Heat oil in a wide pan.
Using a coconut shell with a small hole, drizzle batter in a lace pattern.
Fry until crispy. Remove and drain.
Warm treacle with cinnamon and food coloring.
Drizzle syrup over the lace and let it set.

recipes.name: Lump Rice (Lamprais)
recipes.shortDescription: Dutch-influenced Sri Lankan rice dish — meat, sambol, and rice baked in a banana leaf.
steps: Prepare the curry, sambol, and meatballs separately.
Lay out banana leaves and place a portion of rice in the center.
Top with curry, sambol, meatballs, and egg.
Wrap tightly into a parcel and secure with string.
Bake at 180°C for 25–30 minutes.
Open carefully and serve hot.

recipes.name: Brinjal Moju
recipes.shortDescription: Sweet, sour, and spicy eggplant pickle — a festive must-have.
steps: Slice brinjals and soak in salted water for 10 minutes.
Pat dry and deep-fry until golden brown.
In a pan, sauté onion, chilies, and ginger-garlic.
Add chili powder, turmeric, vinegar, sugar, and salt.
Add fried brinjals and toss gently.
Simmer until the sauce coats the brinjals. Cool and serve.
